interactions.label: In India, smoked tobacco is a more significant risk factor for oral cancer than

params.question: In India, smoked tobacco is a more significant risk factor for oral cancer than smokeless tobacco products such as gutka and khaini.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Actually, smokeless tobacco is the bigger threat in India. Gutka, khaini, and mishri involve prolonged direct mucosal contact, unlike the brief exposure from smoke. Combined with areca nut — classified by IARC as a Group 1 carcinogen — the risk is multiplicative.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. In India, smokeless tobacco products (gutka, khaini, mishri) are the dominant oral carcinogens, not smoked tobacco. Prolonged direct mucosal contact and combination with areca nut — an IARC Group 1 carcinogen — produce a multiplicative carcinogenic effect.

interactions.label: A 35-year-old woman's gastric biopsy shows signet-ring cells infiltrating indivi

params.question: A 35-year-old woman's gastric biopsy shows signet-ring cells infiltrating individually without gland formation. Unlike intestinal-type gastric carcinoma, this diffuse-type pattern is LEAST likely to involve which of the following?

answers.text: Loss of E-cadherin function encoded by the CDH1 gene

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: E-cadherin loss is the hallmark molecular event in diffuse-type gastric carcinoma. Loss of this cell-adhesion protein allows individual tumour cells to infiltrate without forming glands.

answers.text: Progression through Correa's cascade of stepwise mucosal changes

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Correa's cascade (chronic gastritis → atrophic gastritis → intestinal metaplasia → dysplasia → carcinoma) is the pathway for intestinal-type gastric carcinoma only. Diffuse-type carcinoma arises through E-cadherin loss and does NOT follow this stepwise progression.
Linitis plastica IS the classic gross appearance of diffuse-type carcinoma. Diffuse infiltration by individual cells produces a rigid, thickened stomach wall resembling a leather bottle.

answers.text: A worse prognosis compared to the intestinal type

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Diffuse-type gastric carcinoma does carry a worse prognosis. It strikes younger patients, lacks glandular architecture, and tends to present at a more advanced stage.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember: Correa's cascade (chronic gastritis → intestinal metaplasia → dysplasia → carcinoma) leads specifically to the intestinal type. Diffuse-type carcinoma arises through E-cadherin loss — a completely different mechanism — and does not follow this stepwise progression.

The Lauren classification divides gastric carcinoma into two fundamentally different entities. Intestinal type follows Correa's cascade and forms glands. Diffuse type is driven by E-cadherin loss, does NOT follow Correa's cascade, and carries a worse prognosis.

interactions.label: A young woman with ileocaecal disease has granulomas on biopsy. Which histologic

params.question: A young woman with ileocaecal disease has granulomas on biopsy. Which histological finding most reliably distinguishes intestinal tuberculosis from Crohn disease?

answers.text: Presence of skip lesions with intervening normal bowel

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Skip lesions are characteristic of Crohn disease, not tuberculosis. Patchy involvement with normal bowel between affected segments is a hallmark of Crohn disease.

answers.text: Small, scattered, non-caseating granulomas in the submucosa

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Small, scattered, non-caseating granulomas are the hallmark of Crohn disease. Tuberculosis produces a distinctly different pattern — large and confluent with caseation.

Correct. Intestinal TB produces large, confluent, caseating granulomas, while Crohn disease produces small, non-caseating, scattered granulomas. Caseation is the single most reliable histological distinguishing feature.

Transmural inflammation and fistulae are hallmarks of Crohn disease. TB rarely causes fistulae. This distinction is critical — starting steroids for presumed Crohn in undiagnosed TB can trigger disseminated disease.

overallFeedback.feedback: Focus on granuloma characteristics: TB produces large, confluent, caseating granulomas; Crohn produces small, scattered, non-caseating ones. Also remember that fistulae and skip lesions point to Crohn, while transverse girdle ulcers point to TB.

Caseation in granulomas is the key distinguishing feature. In the Indian context, always exclude TB (via interferon-gamma release assay or biopsy PCR) before starting immunosuppressive therapy for presumed Crohn disease.

interactions.label: On upper GI endoscopy, which feature most reliably distinguishes a malignant gas

params.question: On upper GI endoscopy, which feature most reliably distinguishes a malignant gastric ulcer from a benign peptic ulcer?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: While benign peptic ulcers are typically under 2 cm, size alone is not a reliable distinguishing feature. Both benign and malignant ulcers can vary in diameter.

answers.text: Location along the lesser curvature of the stomach

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The lesser curvature is a common site for both benign peptic ulcers and gastric carcinomas. Location alone does not reliably distinguish the two.

answers.text: Heaped-up nodular margins with interrupted mucosal folds

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. A malignant ulcer shows heaped-up, nodular, irregular margins with a dirty necrotic base, and mucosal folds are interrupted. A benign peptic ulcer has a clean, punched-out crater with mucosal folds that radiate inward and converge at the margin.
Erythema and oedema are non-specific inflammatory findings seen around both benign and malignant ulcers. They cannot reliably distinguish the two.

overallFeedback.feedback: The key is in the margins and folds. Benign: clean punched-out crater, mucosal folds radiating inward and converging at the edge. Malignant: heaped nodular margins, necrotic base, interrupted folds. Every gastric ulcer must be biopsied — edges and base.

The margin and mucosal fold pattern is the most reliable endoscopic distinction. Always biopsy both the edges and base of every gastric ulcer — the four microscopic zones of a chronic peptic ulcer (necrosis → inflammatory infiltrate → granulation tissue → fibrous scar) differ fundamentally from malignant tissue.

interactions.label: An elderly woman presents with iron-deficiency anaemia and a positive faecal occ

params.question: An elderly woman presents with iron-deficiency anaemia and a positive faecal occult blood test but no visible rectal bleeding or change in bowel habit. Where is her colorectal cancer most likely located?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Rectal cancers typically present with frank rectal bleeding, tenesmus, and altered bowel habit — not occult anaemia. The narrow rectal lumen means symptoms appear early.

Left-sided cancers form napkin-ring strictures in the narrow sigmoid lumen, causing early obstruction, pencil-thin stools, and frank rectal bleeding — a very different presentation from occult anaemia.

Correct. Right-sided cancers grow as polypoid, fungating masses in the wide caecum. The wide lumen allows slow, occult bleeding causing iron-deficiency anaemia without obstruction or visible blood. A palpable right iliac fossa mass may be the only finding.

While transverse colon cancers can present variably, the classic combination of occult bleeding with anaemia and no obstruction is most characteristic of right-sided tumours due to the wider caecal lumen.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember the anatomy: right colon = wide lumen → polypoid mass → occult bleeding → anaemia. Left colon = narrow lumen → napkin-ring stricture → obstruction, pencil stools, and frank bleeding. The anatomy dictates the clinical presentation.

Anatomy determines presentation. The wide right colon tolerates a polypoid mass that bleeds slowly, causing anaemia. The narrow left colon is quickly obstructed by a napkin-ring stricture. Iron-deficiency anaemia in an elderly patient warrants colonoscopy to exclude right-sided colorectal cancer.
